newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Media concentration plan set to resurface.
newsitem.headline: Media concentration plan set to resurface.

text.p: A European Commission draft directive aimed at guaranteeing a single market and pluralism in the media is set to resurface this week, after six months of germination, EU officials said.
Commissioners' chief aides will on Wednesday seek to prepare the draft text for adoption a week later on March 12.
Officials said the text did not differ largely from the proposal first mulled last September, under which the audience share of media groupings would be capped with the goal of preserving pluralism.

The Commission has drawn up its proposal with the aim of meeting the European Parliament's demands for a directive protecting pluralism in the media at the time of media mega mergers and concentrations in the style of Italian media mogul Silvio Berlusconi and Australia's Rupert Murdoch.
The European Newspaper Publishers' Association said on Tuesday that as there had been no fundamental reconsideration of the September 1996 text, its previous reservations remained.

It argued in a statement that the the development of the information society required press companies in Europe, whatever their size and location, to be able to become truly multimedia companies and to invest in cross-media ventures.
It said that existing EU competition rules were sufficient to guarantee media pluralism and that guaranteeing pluralism is not anyway within the remit of the EU.

The Commission was divided last September when it discussed the text on media concentrations presented by Internal Market Commissioner Mario Monti. The text proposed limiting the market shares of single media such as newspapers, radio or television stations to 30 percent, while groups crossing more than one media would see each strand limited to an average of 10 percent.
